ready1_open_rewrite.title: GeoSQA Open-ended Question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The land-atmosphere system (atmosphere and ground) absorbs solar shortwave radiation (energy income), and also emits longwave radiation outward (energy expenditure). The difference between energy income and expenditure is called the radiation balance. The figure below is a monthly distribution chart of the multi-year average radiation balance of a certain coastal place. Read the figure and answer: Although the annual total radiation balance of this place is a negative value, the annual average temperature has not declined year by year. This is related to the influence of which factors? <image1>
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Factors such as atmospheric circulation and ocean circulation

The multi-year average radiation balance of this place is mostly negative in winter and late autumn to early winter; about January—March and September—December are deficits; around April—July it is positive, reaching the maximum near July; near August it is close to 0. The land-atmosphere system (atmosphere and ground) absorbs solar shortwave radiation (energy income), and also emits longwave radiation outward (energy expenditure). The difference between energy income and expenditure is called the radiation balance. The figure below is a monthly distribution chart of the multi-year average radiation balance of a certain coastal place. Read the figure and answer: Although the annual total radiation balance of this place is a negative value, the annual average temperature has not declined year by year. This is related to the influence of which factors?

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows: The horizontal axis is months 1—12, and the vertical axis is radiation balance. Above the 0 line indicates radiation surplus, and below the 0 line indicates radiation deficit. The multi-year average radiation balance of this place is mostly negative in winter and late autumn to early winter; about January—March and September—December are deficits; around April—July it is positive, reaching the maximum near July; near August it is close to 0. Overall, there are many negative-value months and the deficit area is relatively large, so the annual total radiation balance is negative. Reasoning: If only the radiation income and expenditure of the local land-atmosphere system are considered, a long-term net deficit would make the temperature decline year by year; but the question stem states that the annual average temperature has not declined year by year, indicating that this place has also obtained heat compensation from outside. Heat exchange in coastal areas is significant, and external heat is mainly transported through atmospheric motion and seawater motion, so it is related to the influence of factors such as atmospheric circulation and ocean circulation.
